newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Astra's Q1 profits disappoint market.
newsitem.headline: Astra's Q1 profits disappoint market.

text.p: Swedish drugs company Astra on Monday posted a lower-than-expected profit for the first three months of 1997, saying stockpiling prior to the end of 1996 had wiped 400 million crowns off sales.
Astra said its first quarter pre-tax profit edged up just one percent to 3.46 billion crowns ($453.1 million) while analysts had expected a profit of 3.93 billion crowns.
Sales rose nine percent in the three months ending March 31 to 10.13 billion crowns but were hit by some stockpiling by patients and wholesalers prior the end of 1996.
"It had an effect of about 400 million crowns on sales," said Astra's spokesman Staffan Ternby, without saying exactly how large of an effect the stockpiling had had on profits.
The result disappointed the market and Astra's shares tumbled 22 crowns to close at 320.5 crowns.
Ternby said sales had been unusually high last November and December, affecting sales in the first quarter this year.
"But the fundamental underlying factors are still positive," he told Reuters, however noting that the market had weakened more than expected and that it was hard to say if this would continue.
"It is hard to know but there is nothing fundamentally that backs this up. There is no crisis or anything," he said.
In the first quarter, Astra posted a 14 percent rise in its own sales of blockbuster anti-ulcer treatment Losec to 4.80 billion crowns.
Astra's total world sales rose to 7.05 billion crowns from 5.90 billion.
Sales of Astra's second biggest selling drug, the anti-asthma agent Pulmicort, rose nine percent to 1.21 billion crowns.
Astra's third main product, beta-blocker Seloken, its largest product in the cardiovascular area, gained four percent to 638 million crowns.
Astra's sales in Europe rose to 5.60 billion crowns from 5.49 billion while North American sales rose to 2.94 billion crowns from 2.46 billion crowns.
-- Belinda Goldsmith, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1045 ($ = 7.635 Swedish Crowns)
